mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near its current depressed level instead of recovering, weekday foot traffic will remain weak and RETAIL_REC will stay below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is still about -9.0 to -9.0 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while WORKPLACES remains at or below -9 for most of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in TRANSIT below its recent levels will reduce spontaneous shopping trips and city-centre visitation, pulling RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 week-on-week and stays there
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -42.0 to -32.7 but remains deeply negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases for two consecutive weeks even though TRANSIT drops back below -35 or remains below that threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve together, the combined return of commuting and in-person activity will raise retail exposure and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series moved upward in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its previous four-week average after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay suppressed, the city is still in a stay-at-home pattern that diverts spending away from retail venues and keeps RETAIL_REC weak.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is above baseline while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying positive and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES staying below zero.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after its recent dip will draw discretionary outings into outdoor leisure instead of shopping districts, reducing retail visits during the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from 5.0 to -18.6 and then partially recovered to -15.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases immediately after PARKS posts a week-on-week rise of 10 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps recovering while RETAIL_REC remains weak, households are satisfying errands locally rather than making broader shopping trips, so retail-and-recreation mobility will stay below the prior month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -5.4 to -1.9 while RETAIL_REC stayed near -12
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean even as GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve or stays less negative.

mechanism_narrative: Under a reopening regime, the recent narrowing in the gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should translate into more mall and restaurant traffic, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both measures improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve after TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS stops falling and returns toward positive territory after a week of recovery, the same mobility impulse will spill into nearby retail areas and lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above -10 after having been below -10 the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -18.6 to -11.1 before slipping to -15.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next month after PARKS crosses above -10.
